anti_overlap: Leave the composition arithmetic to the composition-focused reviewer — how wing bias, roster kill-share heredity, and the pace/aggression/thoroughness playstyle axes combine into one hatch outcome, which signal the player credits, and the determinism-versus-legibility band. This review stops at what the bins are, how they are cut, and how many there should be.
Do not review PixiJS colony rendering, the persistence/localStorage schema, Beat 2 zone or mood systems, or the incubation ceremony's UX; those are separate slices of the same brainstorm.

Do not re-litigate decisions the brainstorm already ruled (pick-of-3 at extraction, incubation across the next run, options-not-power coupling, procedural rendering) unless a wing-set choice specifically breaks one of them.

Do not report engineering-quality issues in src/sim/habitat/encryptidMatcher.ts such as console logging or class structure; only its scoring semantics matter here, and only insofar as they constrain which axis is computable.
decision_lens: Could a player, shown only what the run produced and told nothing, name the wing — and would a novice reach that point after the number of exposures a Beat 1 play session actually affords? A bin that cannot be named blind is decoration on top of a mapping, not a taxonomy; a bin encountered too rarely to train on is a name the player will never attach to a feeling.
distance_rationale: Perfumery shares no parent discipline with game design, library science, or software architecture, yet its central unsolved problem for four centuries is exactly the one this design faces: a continuous perceptual field must be cut into a small set of named bins that ordinary people can learn by exposure alone. Perfumery has argued the same axis fight in public and in print — should a family be named by the material it contains, by the impression it leaves, by the occasion it serves, or by descent from one seminal formula — and has empirical answers about how many bins a untrained nose can hold and how often a bin must be encountered before it becomes discriminable. Because the discipline classifies smells, not stories or records, it carries none of the Borgesian-library or bestiary associations that would make the reviewer echo the design's own vocabulary back at it.
expected_isomorphisms: wing ↔ olfactive family (a perceptual bin, not an ontological one). The axis fight ↔ perfumery's unresolved mix of ingredient-named families (woody, floral), impression-named families (fresh, oriental), and lineage-named families (fougère and chypre are named after single 19th-century products, not descriptors) — the same silent axis-mixing the straw wing set may contain. Wing count ↔ the Fragrance Wheel's 4 families / 14 subfamilies and its repeated revisions, where new bins were forced into existence because buyers could not place aquatics anywhere — evidence that count is set by discriminability, not tidiness. Literacy through repetition ↔ nose training against reference standards: a family smelled twice a year never becomes a category. Composing several signals ↔ the accord and the top/heart/base pyramid, where which note is perceived first governs what the wearer credits the scent to. The ~99 roster creatures in no family ↔ orphan materials that fit no family, and the specific anosmias where a whole family is invisible to a fraction of noses. Two consumers ↔ the durable split between the retail wheel a buyer navigates by and the formula/olfactive-pyramid a perfumer composes by, which the trade keeps as two cross-referenced systems rather than forcing into one.
focus: Whether the wing set is cut on a single coherent axis, whether that axis is computable from facts the game actually records, whether five bins are discriminable and learnable at the encounter rate Beat 1 affords, and whether one classification can serve both hatch-mapping and later loot-targeting or whether the honest answer is two cross-referenced systems.
name: fd-perfumery-family-legibility
persona: Apply the perspective of a perfumery classification specialist — someone who trains noses against reference standards and who has watched fragrance-family schemes be revised because buyers could not place a scent, could not tell two families apart, or learned a bin name without ever learning to recognize the bin. This perspective treats a category as real only when someone can name it blind from the evidence alone, holds that the number of categories is set by how many a novice can discriminate rather than by how many the corpus suggests, and is habitually suspicious of taxonomies whose bins are named on different axes without anyone noticing. It reads the underlying corpus rationales before trusting any category name, and it separates the classification a customer navigates by from the classification a maker composes by.
review_areas: Axis coherence — check whether the five straw wings are cut on one axis or several silently mixed. Funerary, Tempest, and Hearth read as tonal impression; Mirrors reads as a behavioral predicate (deception); Hungers reads as an appetite relation to the player. Test each candidate axis from the goal (record type per §11.6, eidogen dimension cluster, media-feature region, enemy ecology, player-verb affordance) against the actual `rationale` strings and member lists in families.json and the blurbs in families-prose.yaml, not against family names — the families were produced by clustering with recorded rationales, and several rationales cut across the straw wings.

Coverage and residue — measure the straw set against the real corpus rather than the summary: which of the 44 families each wing claims, how many creatures those pools actually contain, how many of the 44 families no wing claims, and what becomes of roster creatures that belong to no family at all. Quantify the gap between total family membership and the 645-creature roster and say what the design must do with it.

Discriminability and the exposure budget — estimate encounters per wing at plausible Beat 1 run lengths and session lengths (ground the estimate in the formation doc and the teardowns doc, not in assumption), then judge whether five bins can be learned at that rate. Flag any pair of wings whose evidence to the player is so similar that they will be conflated regardless of how distinct the underlying pools are.

Two-consumer fracture — assess whether hatch-mapping (an impression read backward at extraction) and loot-farming literacy (a targeting decision made forward, before the run) want the same bins. Evaluate the option the design has not stated: keep one taxonomy plus an explicit cross-reference to the other, as the trade does with the retail wheel and the perfumer's pyramid, and say which should be primary in Beat 1.

Computability from recorded facts — check that whichever axis is recommended can be derived from what RunReport.ts actually exposes and what MediaFeatures in src/sim/habitat/types.ts actually carries (entropy, rhythm, emotionalTone, colorPalette, keywords). An axis that needs a fact the run never records makes wing identity an arbitrary label rather than a mapping.
Naming versus delivery — whether wing names promise a discrimination the pools cannot deliver, so the shown justification text reads as arbitrary even where the underlying mapping is sound.

severity_examples.condition: Escalate to P0 when the axis is unreachable from RunReport.ts facts and MediaFeatures fields combined, because every downstream design decision — hatch legibility, literacy, later loot targeting — rests on the mapping being real.
severity_examples.scenario: The recommended or straw taxonomy axis cannot be computed from any fact the run records, so the wing announced at delve start bears no derivable relation to what the run produced and the 'this run became this creature' claim is a post-hoc label pasted onto an unrelated roll.

severity_examples.condition: P1 rather than P2 when the conflation is structural (shared families or indistinguishable evidence) rather than a naming problem fixable by copy.
severity_examples.scenario: Two of the five wings draw from family pools that overlap heavily or produce hatches a player cannot tell apart, so at the encounter rate Beat 1 affords the player never forms the distinction and the wing vocabulary stays inert.

Wing names carry a tonal register the family rationales and blurbs do not support, so the pick-of-3 justification reads as arbitrary to the player even though the underlying pool assignment is defensible.

source_domain: Perfumery — olfactive family classification and accord construction: the Grasse/Osmothèque tradition of reference standards and nose training, the Fragrance Wheel and its successive revisions, and the top/heart/base pyramid.
success_hints: Open /Users/sma/projects/jawnomicon/exports/families/v16/families.json and count actual member lists before accepting any claim about pool size — family sizes range from 3 to 21 members and the sum across all 44 families is smaller than the stated 645-creature roster. Report the arithmetic.

Read the `rationale` field in families.json alongside the blurbs in /Users/sma/projects/jawnomicon/data/families-prose.yaml. Families were named from clustering rationales (traits, behaviors, provenance), and whether a tonal wing is a coherent union of those rationales is checkable rather than a matter of taste.

Convert literacy into numbers: estimate delve duration and runs-per-session from game-design-docs/after-them-delve-formation.md and docs/research/2026-08-09-meta-home-loop-teardowns.md, then state expected encounters per wing per session at 3, 5, and 7 wings so the count question is decided against a curve rather than an intuition.

Propose at least one concrete alternative wing set with its pools enumerated from the real family list, not just a critique of the straw set. A named alternative with coverage numbers is far more useful than an axis argument in the abstract.

Where the two consumers genuinely pull apart, say which one Beat 1 should serve, what the cross-reference to the other looks like, and what it would cost to add the second system later — the design explicitly defers full Borgesrooms, so the cost of deferral is the decision.
task_context:
Ideate and evaluate alternatives for the Borgesroom wing-set v0 in After Them — the themed wing identity each delve run rolls, which biases the encryptid matcher's family pools and makes run→creature hatching legible ('this run became this creature'). The current straw proposal is five tonal wings mapped to jawnomicon families: Funerary (Death-Criers/Underworld Court/Night-Comers), Tempest (Tempest-Bringers/Rain-Serpents/Rain-Holders/Maelstrom-Makers), Hearth (Hearth-Bound/Kindly Watchers/Blessing-Bearers/First Teachers), Hungers (Lurking Hunters/Hungers That Think/Monstrous Broods/Wings of Ill Omen), Mirrors (Tricksters/Shape-Thieves/Never-Caught). Evaluate and propose better alternatives on four questions: (1) Is wing-as-tonal-theme the right taxonomy axis at all? Consider alternatives: wings by record type (canon §11.6: 'funerary wings lean funerary records' — wings are archive sections of a Borgesian library), by eidogen dimension cluster, by media-feature region (entropy/rhythm/emotionalTone), by enemy ecology, by player-verb affordance. (2) Is five the right count for Beat 1, given each wing must be felt often enough to build literacy? (3) How should wing bias compose with the other hatch signals (roster kill-share heredity, pace/aggression/thoroughness playstyle axes) so hatches stay legible but not deterministic — and never hard-gate the 645-creature roster? (4) The wings will serve TWO consumers — hatch mapping now, loot-farming literacy later (§11.6) — do the two jobs pull toward different taxonomies, and if so which taxonomy serves both? Ground in the actual sources, do not trust summaries: docs/research/2026-08-09-meta-home-loop-teardowns.md, game-design-docs/teardown-arpg-modifiers.md §11-12, game-design-docs/after-them-delve-formation.md (R1-R8), /Users/sma/projects/jawnomicon/exports/families/v16/families.json (44 families with member lists), /Users/sma/projects/jawnomicon/data/families-prose.yaml (family blurbs), src/sim/habitat/types.ts (MediaFeatures), src/sim/habitat/encryptidMatcher.ts (scoring), src/ui/RunReport.ts (available run facts).

The design under review is a brainstorm document at docs/brainstorms/2026-08-09-habitat-place-brainstorm.md; the wing set is its open question 1 and is unresolved. Within that goal, this review covers questions 1, 2, and 4 — the taxonomy axis, the count, and the two-consumer question — and treats question 3 as another reviewer's territory. Findings should be graded P0 (would corrupt or block the whole design), P1 (must fix before implementing), P2 (degrades quality), P3 (polish).
